scorecard.name: Verified customer
scorecard.coaching: Verify the customer's address, PIN, or security question within the first four minutes rather than waiting until [05:33] after only taking the account number and date of birth at [00:20].

scorecard.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
scorecard.coaching: Express sincere empathy and reassurance when the customer shares at [01:29] and [01:50] that he is terrified about having no emergency phone line for his wife's heart condition.

scorecard.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
scorecard.coaching: Remain calm and professional rather than making sarcastic remarks like telling the customer at [09:20] that you cannot control the British weather or stop lightning hitting a pole.

scorecard.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
scorecard.coaching: The customer's fibre broadband and voice line remain completely disconnected at the end of the call ([13:45]), pending an Openreach overhead hoist crew visit in 48 hours.

grader.scenario: Complete loss of overhead fibre broadband and voice line after a thunderstorm damaged a telegraph pole on a rural lane
grader.notes: Owen follows branding, manages his hold properly ([06:03]-[07:32]), probes thoroughly into physical hazard and ONT status, and takes ownership by ordering a 4G backup dongle with an attic antenna ([10:13]). However, he fails verification by only asking for account number and DOB in the first 4 minutes and waiting until [05:33] to ask for the address and PIN, shows zero empathy when Ferdinand is terrified about his wife's heart condition ([01:29]-[02:01]), makes a sarcastic remark about the British weather at [09:20], and the overhead line remains severed pending a 48-hour hoist repair ([13:45]).

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: Greeting at [00:00] ('thank you for calling S-Net') and closing at [14:15] ('thank you for choosing S-Net').

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: Managed 68s hold between [06:03] ('Please bear with me for a moment while I contact their dispatch desk') and [07:32] ('Thank you for holding, Ferdinand').

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: At [00:20] Agent only requested account number and date of birth; property address and PIN were not requested until [05:33] (past the 240s mark).

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: Agent addressed customer by first name 'Ferdinand' throughout ([00:20], [00:37], [02:01], [05:33], [07:32], [14:15]).

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: At [01:29] and [01:50] customer expressed severe distress (-36.0 sentiment) about his wife's heart condition and zero indoor signal; Agent responded coldly and procedurally at [01:40] and [02:01] with zero empathy or apology.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: At [01:18] Agent paraphrased the issue: 'So to summarize, lightning from this morning's storm damaged pole DP-449 on Millbrook Lane and severed your overhead dropwire, leaving both your broadband and landline completely dead.'

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: Agent retained pole number DP-449, Millbrook Lane, attic signal details ([09:53]), and calling from neighbour's phone ([11:24]) without re-asking.

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: At [08:41], [10:13], [10:28], and [12:47], Agent escalated the Openreach hoist slot, personally ordered a free pre-activated 4G backup hub with window antenna, and scheduled a personal follow-up task.

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: At [09:20] Agent snapped sarcastically: "Well, Ferdinand, I obviously can't control the British weather or stop lightning hitting a pole, can I?"

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: Agent probed road obstruction ([02:01]), power cable hazards ([02:22]), dangling cross-arm safety ([02:41]), mains power ([03:01]), ONT LEDs ([03:21]), battery backup alarm ([03:57]), and Hub 5 status ([04:17]).

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: At [08:02] and [13:45], the overhead fibre dropwire and pole DP-449 remain severed awaiting an Openreach hoist crew in 48 hours.
